text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered -> severity P1: high kv-cache growth on runtime pool `us-west-2/gpu-pool-3` causing >3x p95 token latency and streaming stalls. paging oncall.

oncall-sre: I'm on it — grabbing logs and confirming blast radius.

sara: i see continuous-batching spikes around 16:13 UTC, backlog backlog_count spikes to ~12k, and kvcache memory climbs and triggers eviction churn.

devon: attaching tail of runtime logs:```
[16:12:54] kv_cache: insert key=conv:abc123:prefill size=4.9MB total=1.9GB
[16:12:54] speculative_decoder: draft->target sync started token_idx=0
[16:12:55] kv_cache: insert key=conv:abc123:draft:0 size=6.2MB total=2.1GB
[16:12:55] eviction: LRU reclaimed 0 items (insertion failed)
[16:12:56] runtime: request_queue latency p95=420ms p99=1.6s
```

alan: looks like speculative decoding is writing drafts into the KV cache (draft keys) while continuous batching merges similar requests -> duplicate cache entries and eviction storms. draft vs target keys are not being normalized.

mira: customer impact: streaming endpoints for a subset of high-concurrency customers (customer-a, customer-b) saw stalls and a few 503s. CS notified.

cs-lead-julie: we've opened tickets with the impacted accounts and notified them we're investigating; they're seeing increased token latency and aborted streams.

oncall-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable speculative-to-kv writes, 2) reduce batch concurrency cap, 3) restart a small canary of runtime nodes with config changes. can anyone flip the feature flag?

sara: I can flip the FF in prod config manager — flag name `speculative.decode.write_to_kv` (default true). Prepared patch to set false.

devon: I'll prepare a hotfix for batching config: set `continuous_batching.max_concurrency=32` and `continuous_batching.max_batch_size=64` for affected pool. We should also set `kv_cache.write_mode=target-only` if supported.

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy plan created: rollback speculative KV writes -> patch cfg 1776001234-hotfix. 3-step rollout: canary 2 nodes, monitor 5m, scale to pool.

alan: quick check: is there any risk disabling speculative writes will regress latency for low-latency clients? We should warn CS.

mira: yes slight increase in average latency for some prompts but p95 should drop once eviction stops. CS, please let affected customers know there's a small tradeoff but overall stability improves.

oncall-sre: executing changes now. sara, flip flag and confirm. devon, apply batching patch. I'll kick off canary restarts.

sara: flag flipped -> `speculative.decode.write_to_kv=false` (applied to pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-3).

devon: batching config patched and rolled to canary nodes. kubectl commands:```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/gpu-runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_MAX_CONCURRENCY=32
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/gpu-runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=64
```

oncall-sre: canary restart: `kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-runtime -n runtime --selector=canary=true`

eng-runtime-bot: Canary status: 2/2 pods ready. healthcheck OK. p95 down from 420ms -> 140ms on canary. no increase in errors observed.

mira: checking customer telemetry: customer-a latency back to baseline, customer-b still showing a bit of tail but trending down. No further 503s in last 10m.

alan: logs now show fewer duplicate kv keys and no eviction churn. sample:```
[16:22:14] kv_cache: insert key=conv:abc123:target size=4.8MB total=1.1GB
[16:22:15] runtime: request_queue latency p95=130ms p99=420ms
```

cs-lead-julie: I'll send a short update to customers acknowledging the mitigation and estimated ETA for full restore.

oncall-sre: scaling rollout to remaining nodes now. monitoring for memory regression and tail latency. Would like a brief handoff to next oncall in 30m.

sara: full rollout applied to pool. config now set across nodes. Flag disabled across us-west-2/gpu-pool-3.

devon: added a temporary guard in runtime: do not materialize draft keys into kvcache unless draft_to_target_map exists. Will push a follow-up PR to normalize keys on speculative->target merge.

mira: customer impact summary for handoff: impacted customers (customer-a, customer-b) experienced 2-4m of degraded streaming; a small number of requests aborted (rate <0.05%). No data loss. Primary cause: speculative decoding writing draft keys + continuous batching merging similar requests -> cache divergence and eviction blowup.

oncall-sre: Handoff note for next oncall: monitor metrics `kv_cache.size_bytes`, `kv_cache.eviction_rate`, `continuous_batching.queue_length`, `runtime.request_latency_p95`, `streaming.errors`. If eviction_rate spikes again, revert by setting `continuous_batching.max_concurrency=16` and re-enable `kv_cache.read_only=true` for suspected pools.

alan: post-incident actions (short): 1) Add unit/regression test covering speculative decode + batching prefill/draft merge, 2) implement key normalization between draft/target, 3) add canary that simulates heavy speculative writes, 4) add alert threshold on kv_cache insertion rate.

devon: I'll own the key-normalization PR and the batching hotfix follow-up. sara will own the FF audit and toggles. mira + cs to follow up with customers. oncall-sre, please file the incident with timeline.

oncall-sre: filing incident now and will assign postmortem owners. Handoff complete — leaving monitoring in ✅ steady state at 16:55 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved (mitigated). Follow-up: schedule postmortem and remediation tasks within 48h.

sara: thx team — flagging this for postmortem, adding notes to the runbook about speculative-to-kv writes and batching interactions. :thumbsup:

mira: one more note — we should consider a runtime invariant: never write ephemeral/draft objects to shared kvcache unless explicitly deduplicated.

alan: agreed. will propose invariant in postmortem.

eng-runtime-bot: Created issue RNW-3147: "Speculative decode KV write normalization + batching regression tests" assigned to devon.

cs-lead-julie: i'll coordinate follow-up comms with impacted customers tomorrow.

oncall-sre: signing off this shift; next oncall @alan (handoff summary pinned).

alan: thanks — catching up on logs and will monitor for 1h.

(END OF THREAD)
